LH-REG-002.question: An insurer incorporated in Bermuda wants to sell life insurance policies to residents of Ohio. In Ohio, this company is classified as:
LH-REG-002.explanation: An alien insurer is organized under the laws of another country, and Ohio requires it to hold a certificate of authority before transacting business here. A foreign insurer is one incorporated in a different U.S. state, which is the tempting choice but applies only to companies formed within the United States.

LH-PROV-004.explanation: Ohio Revised Code 3915.05(B) requires a grace period of one month for every premium after the first, during which the policy stays in force, and allows the overdue premium to be deducted at settlement. So the insurer pays $100,000 - $1,200 = $98,800, not the full $100,000.

LH-HPRV-001.explanation: Ohio Revised Code 3923.04(C) requires a grace period of at least 10 days for monthly premiums, so coverage continues through June 11 and any unpaid premium can be deducted from a claim. The 7-day minimum applies only to weekly premiums, and 31 days applies to other modes.
